newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NAB buys AUSMAQ electronic service.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NAB buys AUSMAQ electronic service.

text.p: National Bank Australia Ltd said on Thursday it has purchased Australian Market Automated Quotation System (AUSMAQ) Ltd, an electronic trading service, for an undisclosed sum.
NAB spokesman Haydn Park told Reuters details of the transaction were being kept confidentional.

The AUSMAQ system electronically links funds management companies and investment advisers eliminating the need for investors to fill out forms to buy and sell fund management products and some wholesale money market products, Park said.
"The financial planner will have this service and he or she will be able to use it in real time. It's cheaper to use for the investor and gets their money in straight away," Park said.
AUSMAQ currently gives subscribers access to about 100 managed investments at lower costs than equivalent retail products, NAB said in a statement.
Park said the bank aimed to provide all of the managed investments available in Australia via the AUSMAQ system and was working to sign on as many investment intermediaries as possible.
"In Australia, it's only just started," he said.
NAB said it planned to expand AUSMAQ from an Australia-only network to New Zealand and it was researching the feasibility of launching the system in other parts of the world.
Park said AUSMAQ was unlikely to be expanded to compete with stock exchanges as an equities trading system.
Park said NAB's investment in the system was expected to pay itself back "very quickly", but would not estimate likely annual revenues from it.
